channel.title: The Backward Pass by Anirudh Srinivasan
channel.description: First-principles, illustrated deep dives into how modern AI models are built, trained, and scaled.

item.title: The Agent Evaluation Playbook
item.description: How to evaluate agent trajectories, world-state changes, reliability, safety, graders, budgets, and long-horizon failures.

item.title: What Autograd Actually Does
item.description: Backpropagation and autograd from scalar chain rules to Jacobian products, saved tensors, activation memory, and checkpointing.

item.title: Why Transformers Do Not Explode
item.description: Initialization, signal propagation, residual paths, normalization, optimizer dynamics, precision, and training stability.

item.title: Choosing the Next Token
item.description: Temperature, beam search, sampling, truncation, penalties, grammars, and contrastive generation from first principles.

item.title: Teaching a Language Model to Follow Instructions
item.description: Supervised fine-tuning as behavior cloning: data construction, loss masking, distribution shift, and capability change.

item.title: How LoRA Changes a Model Without Rewriting It
item.description: PEFT from first principles: low-rank updates, LoRA, QLoRA, DoRA, adapters, memory costs, and tradeoffs.

item.title: Inside an AI Agent Harness
item.description: Anatomy of an agent harness: context assembly, actions, verification, containment, budgets, event logs, and compaction.

item.title: Memory Is More Than Context
item.description: Agent memory and context engineering as a bounded problem of writing, updating, retrieving, ranking, and forgetting.

item.title: How Multi-Agent Systems Actually Coordinate
item.description: Multi-agent systems through diversity, specialization, communication topology, coordination cost, orchestration, and failure modes.

item.title: Reinforcement Learning for Agents From First Principles
item.description: Reinforcement learning for agents: environments, reward design, credit assignment, horizons, rollout systems, and evaluation.

item.title: How Attention Moves Information
item.description: A first-principles derivation of QKV attention and its evolution through MHA, GQA, sparse, linear, latent, and multimodal forms.

item.title: The Puzzle of Overparameterization
item.description: Double descent, benign overfitting, implicit bias, function space, grokking, and what they do and do not explain about LLM generalization.

item.title: How LLMs Are Pretrained
item.description: How pretraining corpora are acquired, filtered, deduplicated, mixed, tokenized, packed, scheduled, and evaluated.

item.title: Mixing Data Without Losing Capabilities
item.description: Post-training data mixtures, task interference, capability transfer, catastrophic forgetting, and practical mitigation strategies.

item.title: How Language Models Learn to Use Tools
item.description: Tool schemas, function-call training, retrieval over large catalogs, synthetic trajectories, constrained decoding, and executable rewards.

item.title: The Making of an AI Agent
item.description: Agent loops, trajectory data, imitation and reinforcement learning, long-horizon credit assignment, state, harnesses, and environments.

item.title: What Changed Inside the Transformer?
item.description: A first-principles guide to the design pressures that turned the original Transformer into modern dense, MoE, and hybrid language models.

item.title: Scaling Laws from First Principles
item.description: Scaling laws from first principles: compute accounting, compute-optimal allocation, data quality, deployment economics, and empirical planning.

item.title: Reinforcement Learning from First Principles
item.description: Policy gradients, baselines, advantages, GAE, trust regions, and PPO derived and translated into language-model rollouts.

item.title: Teaching a Model What We Prefer: From RLHF to DPO
item.description: How comparisons become rewards, why RLHF uses a reference-policy KL, and how the objective becomes DPO.

item.title: How Reinforcement Learning Teaches Models to Reason
item.description: RLVR, verifiers, GRPO, DeepSeek-R1, exploration, and the engineering lessons from open reasoning-model replications.

item.title: Thinking in Tokens: What Reasoning Models Actually Do
item.description: How reasoning tokens provide serial compute, support search and refinement, and sometimes lead to overthinking.

item.title: How Models Improve Without Changing Their Weights
item.description: How to allocate inference compute across longer chains, sampling, search, and verification under per-prompt budgets.

item.title: How to Find What Is Slowing Your Model
item.description: A practical guide to profiling ML systems with timelines, GPU counters, Roofline analysis, PyTorch Profiler, Nsight, and bottleneck-driven optimization.

item.title: The Serving Playbook: How LLM and VLM Serving Systems Keep GPUs Busy
item.description: A first-principles guide to continuous batching, paged KV, prefix caching, chunked prefill, disaggregation, speculative decoding, and serving goodput.

item.title: The Mechanics of LLM Inference
item.description: A first-principles guide to autoregressive inference, prefill, decode, KV cache, batching, bandwidth, latency metrics, quantization, and VLM workloads.

item.title: The Parallelism Playbook: How Large Models Train Across Clusters
item.description: A first-principles guide to DDP, ZeRO/FSDP, tensor, pipeline, context, expert, and hybrid parallelism.

item.title: Inside a Training Step
item.description: A first-principles walkthrough of transformer training: tensor shapes, forward and backward passes, FLOPs, activation lifetimes, memory accounting, and checkpointing.

item.title: Talk Is Not Cheap: Communication from PCIe to InfiniBand
item.description: A first-principles guide to PCIe, NVLink, NVSwitch, RDMA, InfiniBand, topology, collective communication, and overlap.

item.title: Why Fast GPUs Still Wait for Memory
item.description: Arithmetic intensity and the Roofline model derived from first principles and applied to GEMM, attention, fusion, optimizers, and ML kernels.

item.title: Why GPUs Are Built for Deep Learning
item.description: Why CPUs and GPUs spend silicon differently, from forms of parallelism and execution hierarchy to latency hiding, memory access, tiling, and Tensor Cores.

item.title: The VLM Architecture Gallery
item.description: Seventy-one vision-language model architectures on one standardized plate, from gated cross-attention to encoders absorbed into the base model.

item.title: Inside a Modern Vision Encoder
item.description: What changed in the visual half of VLMs: intake geometry, resolution, objectives, connectors, and the encoders models actually ship.

item.title: One Transformer, Two Modalities
item.description: A block-by-block comparison of language Transformers and Vision Transformers.

item.title: An Image Is a Sentence: How Vision Transformers See
item.description: An interactive field guide to ViT, DeiT, PVT, Swin, CvT, ConViT, CoAtNet, MViT, TimeSformer, and ViViT.

item.title: Across the CNNVerse
item.description: A visual field guide to convolution and the lineage from LeNet through ResNet, EfficientNet, and ConvNeXt.

item.title: Evolution of ML Architectures
item.description: Sixty-seven years of neural architectures, information flow, training cost, inference state, and gradient paths.

item.title: How Models Know Where They Are
item.description: Absolute, sinusoidal, relative, RoPE, NoPE, 2D and Fourier position features, and multimodal M-RoPE explained visually.

item.title: What an Optimizer Actually Does
item.description: A mechanical tour from SGD to Muon: optimizer updates, state costs, and distributed training bottlenecks.

item.title: The Geometry of Normalization
item.description: Normalization from BatchNorm to Peri-LN, including why the modality interface in a VLM is a normalization problem.

item.title: Why Neural Networks Need Nonlinearity
item.description: From sigmoid and ReLU to GELU, SwiGLU, and squared ReLU, with animated derivations and model comparisons.
